items.note: Hessel Bottom named as the wet meadow at Ostrey Hollow; 'six farms' affirmed as the solid farm count; Emmet Brant 'biggest herd in Hessel Bottom'.
Brant's private weigh book from 1 Jan 1897 and the two agreeing scales appear nowhere in Section A.

Complaints from March 1902 that Hollow milk 'runs poorer than theirs down the valley'. No Hollow-vs-Green gap stated as 0.19 and no Larrow Green average derived from it, so the disqualifier does not fire.
Grigg's 1908 wet-hay finding is named and correctly framed as a finding, but the bolded Jan-Feb-Mar 1908 sampling window is absent from Section A.
No Brant 1910 year (200,000 lb at a recorded 3.42) and no proportional-loss point.
No Roy Brant, no 1929 succession, no 1958 loan of the book to Ivy Keddie.
Alder Corners, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd appear nowhere in the run's Section A.
No four patrons hauling to the cheese factory in the summer flush from 1915.
REQUIRED independence (two of four elements) not stated; the comparison is never mentioned.
No 0.19-higher Alder Corners test, no sixteen seasons 1915-1930.
The same-milk-two-buildings argument is absent from Section A.
No Rosalie Cudd, no 1958 copying of sixteen seasons for Ivy Keddie.
Merle Strawn is named only as 'the inspector'; the Ordell circuit, the 1907-1936 span and his independence are absent from Section A.
No lactometer checks on every visit and no 'never found added water at Ostrey Hollow'.

'On 12 June 1923 the inspector Merle Strawn condemned the Ostrey Hollow station's testing glass' - correct date and the whole lot condemned. The burette is unstated but the item carries no REQUIRED line and the core fact is present.
States that Strawn 'drew no inference whatever' (unbolded context in the key) but never the bolded element: that he wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.

Only 'a replacement order went to the supply house at Tarnet; new glass in by July 1923'. No 28 June order, no 2 July acknowledgment, no 1924 average of 3.80, no failure to connect the rise with the condemnation.

The condemned crate went up the ladder into the station loft in 1923 - the item's own aspect. The notebooks / state office / 1947 college library half is absent, but the item prints no both-required line.
Gives 1,436,000 lb credited, from a self-invented 3.59 (= 3.78 - 0.19). Key: 40,000,000 x 3.61% = 1,444,000 lb. Exact-match item.
Gives 1,512,000 lb delivered from a 3.78 'true average'. Key: 40,000,000 x 3.80% = 1,520,000 lb. Exact-match item.

Difference stated as exactly 76,000 lb, and both denominators are explicitly named and kept apart: 'the tests ran 5.0% low - the patrons were credited with 95% of the fat they delivered' and 'owed 5.25% more than they were paid'. Its computed 5.03 / 5.29 are off because of the wrong bases, but the required difference and the named denominators are right, and it does not claim 5.26 percent of the true fat (no NT-20).
Answers $77.39 (the planted NT-14 value); key is $77.93. Hedged as 'probable, not settled', so no corruption deduction, but no credit.
0.88 c.c. short is right, but the pipette count is declined ('cannot be determined'). Key requires 72 pipettes (6 dozen) AND 0.88 c.c.; this is not an abstention item, so declining loses it.

Both figures are right (26 years and about six weeks, 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923; 25 full delivery years) but the required reason for the difference is wrong: the run says the money window is the 1900-1925 grievance span, explicitly omitting 1897-1900 and including mid-1923-1925, instead of 1898-1922 with 1897 and 1923 excluded as part years.

ABSTENTION A02 correctly declined: 'Pounds of milk received in the first season: cannot be determined from the sources', with what can be said (a part season, therefore below 1,600,000 lb). No figure asserted.
Names the variable: the station's own measure broke 8 May 1911, a borrowed one used until 10 July, 'the only thing changed was the apparatus'.
Constants given well past three: same herds and cows, same patrons, same wet hay of the same bottom, same building, same procedure, same tester.

Nine weeks and the 10 July same-day fall-back are right, but the result is given only qualitatively ('markedly higher', 'fell back'). The bolded averages 3.80 through the interval and 3.61 on return are never stated; the run explicitly says the interval yields 'no quantity'.

Both halves. Establishes: locates the fault in the instrument and rules out herd, feed and men. Limits: no magnitude (not 0.19, not 0.88 c.c.), and does not identify which article of glass was at fault.

Four reasons, three of them valid and distinct with named sources drawn from more than three narrators: the ledger 'station gain' (Association's own books), the 1911 swap (Duncan Keddie R18 anchored by R24), Strawn's 12 June 1923 condemnation (Falke R22).

Independence argued explicitly (different decades, different observers, different kinds of evidence, no common informant), and names the survivors if the 1958 measurement had never happened - reasons 1, 2 and 3, with the ledger surplus ranked strongest because it needs no instrument.

ABSTENTION A09 ASSERTED. Headline verdict sentence in the sheet's own voice: 'no - nobody in the office ever put the question, before 1958.' The later hedging is about a different sub-question (whether the bookkeeper authored the accusation) and does not undo it. -2 applied.

Answers the literal question yes - 'Did he know the station's tests ran low? Yes, certainly' - carried by the 1919 circular over the manager's name and the quarter-century of annual-meeting complaints.

REQUIRED any three of five; only two are present - he signed the annual ledger sheets carrying the station-gain line, and he wrote the 1919 water circular. Missing: manager from 1913 (the run says he is unnamed throughout and gives no start date), that he argued watering at the 1925 hearing, and that nothing in his hand anywhere names the station's glassware.

ABSTENTION A03 correctly declined. Verdict sentence is 'cannot be determined from the sources' for whether he knew the cause was the glass; leaning ('probably not') without deciding is a correct abstention. Two supporting observations present: no source records him being told, asked or answering; and the signature demonstrates opportunity and possession of the evidence, not knowledge of what it meant. No -2.

deductions.reason: Asserts the planted 'eleven families' circular reach (F058) as fact in Section A - 'He carried them by hand to eleven families' - and adopts it in its own resolution as the true door count ('eleven households'). The correct value is nine; the closing 'I do not claim it as proven' attaches to the three-way reconciliation, not to the narrative assertion.
Gullibility: abstention item A09 (D2 item 3) answered with a definite verdict - 'no - nobody in the office ever put the question, before 1958.'
